title: Problem with clothes
author: MMPhotoshop
selftext:
I must admit that, in all my years of programming and solving computing problems, I have never encountered a problem this difficult.

Here is the current result—I’ll be improving it shortly.



I’ve never understood how people manage to create custom clothing for video games.

The situation is so dire that I had to get Codex 6.1 Sol Ultra to collaborate with Claude Code just to get the outfit you see here—all after developing a Blender add-on that is still being refined.



I’ve spent hundreds of euros—I’m not joking—and yet, no one can seem to get an outfit applied correctly. I’ve looked for tutorials, but they’re impossible to follow. I tried using MetaTailor, but they require a subscription to export files; I even tried to pay, but they reject certain types of credit cards in the U.S., so I can’t sign up.



I have no idea how others have been handling clothing until now, but I’m spending way too much—hundreds and hundreds of euros—to get this done. And on top of that, I still have to do manual work, so it’s not even automated.

https://i.redd.it/37dud6v36k0i1.png

comments.author: kokutouchichi
comments.body:
Jesus Christ hundreds of euros or you could you know just spend 20 bucks and get an add on for blender that comes with dozens of base mesh clothing that you can tailor and make and drape yourself. Or buy marvelous designer and make AAA clothing. Im absolutely flabbergasted at how much people are blowing on LLMs to do stuff like this when there are super cheap alternatives or free that do much better and take maybe a couple hours at best to learn.

Here are the basics:

Underlying model your base mesh. Make sure it's all weight painted and rigged. 

Put some clothes on your mesh and use the sculpt tools to push and pull it into place so it covers your mesh like clothes.

Parent the clothes to the rig.

Copy the weights from your base mesh to the clothing.

DoNe!

Or pay me 100 bucks I'll do it for you!

replies.author: MMPhotoshop
replies.body: I want a system that makes me independent and that is always free for me. I don't want to spend money on marvelous designers. Now I want to try on Blender with a common mesh, I'm going crazy. I sound stupid, but I actually created a city the size of GTA San Andreas that is 100% explorable.  So you can also go to the bathrooms of the houses to wash your hands, but this clothes thing is super difficult for me.
